intent.raw_query: Costa Rica eco-adventure, $2500, zip-lining and wildlife, February 2026 from Miami

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits. With over 13 cables and Tarzan swings, you'll glide above the treetops spotting howler monkeys, toucans, and exotic orchids. This iconic eco-adventure combines adrenaline with breathtaking biodiversity in one of the world's most biodiverse regions.

experiences.name: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari
experiences.description: Glide through the jungle canals of Tortuguero on a guided boat safari teeming with wildlife. Spot caimans, river otters, three-toed sloths, poison dart frogs, and over 300 bird species including the great green macaw. If visiting between July and October, witness the awe-inspiring nesting of endangered green sea turtles on the beach at night.

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Nature Hike
experiences.description: Explore Costa Rica's most beloved national park with a certified naturalist guide who will help you spot white-faced capuchin monkeys, two-toed sloths, scarlet macaws, and the rare squirrel monkey. The hike winds through lush rainforest trails leading to stunning Pacific Ocean viewpoints and pristine white-sand beaches, perfectly blending wildlife with natural beauty.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Hot Springs Experience
experiences.description: Walk among the rainforest canopy on a series of suspension bridges offering panoramic views of the iconic Arenal Volcano and surrounding jungle. Spot toucans, morpho butterflies, and howler monkeys from above the forest floor. End the day soaking in natural volcanic hot springs fed by geothermal activity, a uniquely Costa Rican eco-cultural experience.

experiences.name: Osa Peninsula Corcovado Rainforest Expedition
experiences.description: Venture into Corcovado National Park, described by National Geographic as 'the most biologically intense place on Earth.' A full-day guided trek through primary rainforest offers unmatched chances to see tapirs, pumas, harpy eagles, and all four Costa Rican monkey species. This remote, pristine wilderness is the ultimate bucket-list eco-adventure for serious wildlife enthusiasts.
experiences.location: Corcovado National Park, Osa Peninsula, Puntarenas Province

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Costa Rica
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and transit time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 13:00. Clear customs, exchange a small amount of currency at the airport (use ATMs for better rates). Take a budget shuttle or shared bus transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and take a slow walk along the beachfront to get oriented with the surroundings.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the nearby beach town on foot. Visit the local sodas (small Costa Rican eateries) for an authentic and affordable first dinner. Watch the sunset from the beach and relax after your long journey.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a light snack at the airport (~$5–8)
meals.lunch: Grab a quick casado (rice, beans, protein, salad) at an airport or roadside soda (~$6–9)
meals.dinner: Local soda near the resort — try gallo pinto or arroz con pollo (~$7–10)

day_by_day.notes: Do not book any activities for the morning. Use the afternoon purely for arrival logistics. Download the Waze app and save offline maps of Costa Rica. Carry small bills in colones for tips and local purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for a self-guided beachfront walk at sunrise. Look for wildlife along the shoreline — Costa Rica's beaches are home to pelicans, frigatebirds, and occasionally howler monkeys in nearby trees. Enjoy the peaceful morning atmosphere before crowds arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby national park or wildlife refuge accessible from your resort area. Explore trails on foot (many have free or low-cost entry under $5–10). Look for sloths, iguanas, coatis, and tropical birds. Bring water and sunscreen.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the local mercado or street food stalls for dinner. Try patacones (fried plantains), ceviche, or a fresh fruit smoothie (batido). Relax at the resort and plan tomorrow's activities.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or nearby bakery — gallo pinto with eggs (~$4–7)
meals.lunch: Pack snacks from a local pulpería (corner store) for the park — fruit, crackers, water (~$3–5)
meals.dinner: Street food market or local soda — ceviche and patacones (~$8–12)

day_by_day.notes: Wear neutral-colored clothing for wildlife spotting. Bring binoculars if possible — they dramatically improve wildlife viewing. Most national parks open at 8:00 AM.

day_by_day.morning: Book an early morning guided wildlife tour through a local budget operator or hostel notice board — group tours are significantly cheaper than private ones. Look for tours to mangroves or river ecosystems where crocodiles, herons, and kingfishers are commonly spotted.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort area and spend the afternoon at the beach. Rent a bodyboard from a local vendor (~$5–8/hour) or simply swim and snorkel if the water is clear. Look for sea turtles if the season aligns.
day_by_day.evening: Cook a simple meal using groceries from a local supermarket (Super Mas or Pali chain stores are budget-friendly) or dine at a casual beachside restaurant. Try a fresh whole fried fish (pescado entero) which is both affordable and delicious.

meals.breakfast: Gallo pinto with fruit at a local soda (~$4–6)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the tour stop or pack your own sandwiches (~$4–6)
meals.dinner: Beachside casual restaurant — whole fried fish with rice and salad (~$10–14)

day_by_day.notes: Book group wildlife tours at least one day in advance for best prices. Always negotiate politely — many local operators offer discounts for cash payment. Avoid tours that promise guaranteed animal sightings as these may involve unethical practices.

day_by_day.morning: Take a shared shuttle or local bus to a nearby zip-lining operation. Costa Rica is the birthplace of canopy zip-lining and many operators offer budget packages ($35–60) that include multiple cables, a Tarzan swing, and rappelling. Book through a local hostel or online in advance for discounts.
day_by_day.afternoon: After zip-lining, visit a nearby waterfall or natural swimming hole in the area. Many are accessible via short hikes and have little to no entrance fee. Cool off in the fresh water and enjoy the jungle surroundings.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Treat yourself to a moderately priced dinner at a local restaurant to celebrate the day's adventures. Try casado with chicken or fresh fish — a complete and filling Costa Rican meal.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before departure — fruit and toast at the resort or soda (~$4–6)
meals.lunch: Pack lunch or eat at the zip-line operator's café — típico plate (~$6–9)
meals.dinner: Local restaurant near resort — casado with chicken or fish (~$9–13)

day_by_day.notes: Wear closed-toe shoes and comfortable athletic clothing for zip-lining. Secure all loose items — GoPros must be mounted, not handheld. Most operators include helmets and harnesses in the price. Minimum weight requirements typically apply (check in advance).

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local butterfly garden or frog sanctuary — these are extremely popular in Costa Rica and typically cost $10–15 for entry. You'll see dozens of species of poison dart frogs, glass frogs, and morpho butterflies up close. Many offer guided tours included in the price.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local town market or artisan fair. Pick up handmade souvenirs like painted wooden frogs, coffee, or woven bags at fair prices. Practice bargaining respectfully. Visit a local coffee shop and try freshly brewed Costa Rican coffee — some of the best in the world.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or low-cost local cultural event if available (check community boards). Otherwise, enjoy a quiet beach bonfire area or watch the stars from the beach — light pollution is minimal in many Costa Rican coastal areas.

meals.breakfast: Smoothie bowl or fresh tropical fruit plate at a local café (~$4–7)
meals.lunch: Casado at a soda near the butterfly garden (~$6–9)
meals.dinner: Grocery store meal — fresh bread, local cheese, deli meats, and fruit (~$6–9)

day_by_day.notes: February is dry season in most of Costa Rica — expect sunny skies and warm temperatures (28–33°C). Always carry reef-safe sunscreen and a reusable water bottle. Tap water is safe to drink in most of Costa Rica.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget day trip via public bus or shared shuttle to a nearby national park or reserve not yet visited. Costa Rica's bus system (Tica Bus or local MEPE routes) is very affordable ($2–8 per leg). Arrive early to maximize wildlife sightings — animals are most active at dawn.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the national park. Join a ranger-led group walk if available (often free or $5). Look for toucans, scarlet macaws, spider monkeys, and white-faced capuchins. Many parks have clearly marked self-guided trails.
day_by_day.evening: Return by bus before dark. Have a relaxed dinner at a soda near the resort and reflect on the day's wildlife encounters in a travel journal.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before bus — banana and peanut butter sandwich (~$2–3)
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch packed from the grocery store inside the park (~$4–6)
meals.dinner: Soda near resort — sopa negra (black bean soup) and bread (~$6–9)

day_by_day.notes: Check bus schedules the day before — rural routes may only run a few times daily. Always have the return schedule confirmed before departing. Keep a copy of your passport in your bag and leave the original at the resort safe.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recharge day. Sleep in, enjoy a slow breakfast, and spend time on the beach. Use the morning to do laundry (many hostels and budget hotels have laundry facilities for $3–5) and repack your bag for the week ahead.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle from a local shop (~$8–12/day) and explore the surrounding coastal roads and villages. Cycling is a fantastic and eco-friendly way to discover hidden beaches, local farms, and small communities not typically on tourist maps.
day_by_day.evening: Join a free or donation-based beach yoga or meditation session if available in the area (common at Costa Rican beach towns). Finish the evening with a fresh coconut water from a street vendor and a light dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full gallo pinto breakfast with eggs, cheese, and juice at a soda (~$5–7)
meals.lunch: Fresh fruit from a roadside stand and snacks while cycling (~$3–5)
meals.dinner: Vegetarian rice and bean bowl at a health-focused local café (~$7–10)

day_by_day.notes: This is the halfway point of your trip — a rest day prevents burnout and keeps energy high for the second week. Use this day to book any remaining activities for the second half of the trip. Check your budget spending so far and adjust if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Book a white-water rafting experience on a nearby river — Class II–III rapids are ideal for beginners and typically cost $45–75 with a group operator. This is one of Costa Rica's most iconic eco-adventure activities. Many operators include transportation, equipment, and a riverside lunch.
day_by_day.afternoon: After rafting, visit a local organic farm or permaculture project in the area. Many offer free or low-cost tours showing sustainable agriculture, cacao growing, and tropical fruit cultivation. You may get to taste fresh cacao or exotic fruits.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort and enjoy a well-deserved rest. Have dinner at a casual open-air restaurant and try a traditional Olla de Carne (Costa Rican beef and vegetable stew) if available.

meals.breakfast: Early energy breakfast — eggs, toast, and coffee before rafting (~$5–7)
meals.lunch: Riverside lunch provided by rafting operator (usually included) or pack your own (~$0–6)
meals.dinner: Open-air restaurant — Olla de Carne stew with tortillas (~$9–13)

day_by_day.notes: Wear quick-dry clothing for rafting and secure all valuables in waterproof bags. Most operators provide life jackets and helmets. Do not go rafting if you have a recent injury or cannot swim. February water levels may vary — confirm with the operator.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local sea turtle conservation project or wildlife rescue center. Many operate as non-profits and welcome visitors for a small donation ($5–15). You'll learn about Costa Rica's conservation efforts and may get to see rescued animals including toucans, sloths, and monkeys up close.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to a less-visited beach away from the main tourist area. Ask locals for recommendations — Costa Rica has hundreds of beaches, many without crowds. Spend the afternoon swimming, snorkeling, or simply enjoying the pristine natural environment.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset boat tour along the coast — many budget operators offer 1.5-hour sunset cruises for $20–35 that include wildlife spotting (dolphins are common) and a beautiful view of the coastline. Book through your resort or a local operator.

meals.breakfast: Pancakes with tropical fruit at a local café (~$5–8)
meals.lunch: Beachside food shack — fresh ceviche and chips (~$7–10)
meals.dinner: Back at resort area — rice and bean burrito bowl from a casual eatery (~$7–10)

day_by_day.notes: Volunteer opportunities at wildlife rescue centers are sometimes available for free accommodation — inquire if you're interested in extending your stay. Always respect wildlife — no touching, no flash photography, maintain distance as instructed by guides.

day_by_day.morning: Take a guided bird-watching walk at sunrise with a local expert. Costa Rica has over 900 bird species — a knowledgeable guide dramatically increases sightings. Budget guides charge $20–35 for a 2–3 hour walk. Look for resplendent quetzals, scarlet macaws, and toucans.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local waterfall hike. Many of Costa Rica's most spectacular waterfalls require only a 30–60 minute hike and charge minimal entry fees ($2–8). Bring a swimsuit — swimming in the natural pool at the base is a highlight experience.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the local nightlife scene on a budget — many beach towns have free live music at bars on weeknights. Enjoy a local Imperial or Pilsen beer ($1.50–2.50) and socialize with other travelers and locals.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-walk snack — banana and granola bar (~$2–3)
meals.lunch: Post-waterfall meal at a soda near the trailhead — casado (~$7–9)
meals.dinner: Casual bar with free music — bar snacks and drinks (~$8–12)

day_by_day.notes: Bird-watching is best in the first two hours after sunrise. Wear muted colors (no bright red or white) to avoid startling birds. Waterfall trails can be slippery — wear proper hiking sandals or trail shoes. Always tell someone your hiking plans before heading out alone.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning kayaking or stand-up paddleboard (SUP) session in calm coastal waters or a nearby estuary. Rental rates are typically $10–20/hour. Paddle through mangrove tunnels where you can spot crocodiles, herons, and exotic fish in their natural habitat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local chocolate (cacao) workshop or coffee tour. Costa Rica produces world-class cacao and coffee, and many small farms offer 1–2 hour tours for $15–25 that include tastings and the chance to make your own chocolate bar or coffee blend.
day_by_day.evening: Prepare a budget meal at a hostel kitchen if available, using fresh ingredients from a local farmers market. Try cooking gallo pinto yourself — it's simple, delicious, and a great cultural experience. Share the meal with fellow travelers.

meals.breakfast: Yogurt with granola and fresh mango from a local market (~$4–6)
meals.lunch: Snack during the cacao/coffee tour (usually included) plus a light bite (~$3–5)
meals.dinner: Self-cooked gallo pinto with fried egg and avocado (~$4–7)

day_by_day.notes: Mangrove kayaking is one of the most unique eco-experiences in Costa Rica — do not skip it if available in your area. The chocolate workshops make excellent and affordable souvenir purchases — a handmade bar costs $3–6. Stay hydrated throughout all water activities.

day_by_day.morning: Final full-day adventure: book a combo eco-adventure package that includes two or more activities (e.g., zip-lining + hanging bridges + waterfall rappelling). Combo packages are more cost-effective than booking separately and typically run $55–85 for a half-day. This is your last big adventure day — make it count!
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort and spend the afternoon at the beach for a final swim. Reflect on your trip, take final photos, and enjoy the natural beauty of Costa Rica's coastline. Visit any local spots you may have missed during the trip.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a nicer farewell dinner at a mid-range local restaurant — try a seafood platter or traditional Costa Rican feast. Toast to a successful trip with a glass of local guaro sour or a tropical cocktail.

meals.breakfast: Hearty breakfast before the adventure day — eggs, gallo pinto, fruit, coffee (~$6–8)
meals.lunch: Lunch provided by tour operator or at a trailside café (~$5–8)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a slightly nicer local restaurant — seafood platter (~$15–22)

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to also purchase any remaining souvenirs — coffee, hot sauce, artisan crafts, and chocolate are all excellent choices. Avoid airport souvenir shops which charge 2–3x the street price. Pack souvenirs carefully in checked luggage to avoid issues at security.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for one final sunrise on the beach. Take a slow walk, collect a few shells, and say goodbye to the ocean. Enjoy a leisurely last breakfast at your favorite local soda. Begin packing and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort — most checkout times are 11:00 AM (confirm in advance).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your flight time, arrange a shared shuttle or budget bus transfer back to Juan Santamaría International Airport. Arrive at the airport at least 3 hours before your international departure. Use remaining colones on snacks, coffee, or last-minute gifts at the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Costa Rica with incredible memories of zip-lining through jungle canopies, spotting sloths and macaws, swimming in waterfalls, and experiencing the pure life — Pura Vida!

meals.breakfast: Final gallo pinto breakfast at a favorite local soda (~$5–7)
meals.lunch: Airport food or pack snacks from a nearby store before departure (~$5–9)
meals.dinner: On the plane or at a layover airport

day_by_day.notes: Budget tip: If your flight departs late, ask the resort about a late checkout option or luggage storage so you can enjoy a few final hours without your bags. Keep $29 USD cash for the airport departure tax if not already included in your ticket (most modern tickets include it — verify with your airline). Always keep your travel insurance documents accessible. Pura Vida!

trip_options.title: Classic Costa Rica Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits. With over 13 cables and Tarzan swings, you'll glide above the treetops spotting howler monkeys, toucans, and exotic orchids. This iconic eco-adventure combines adrenaline with breathtaking biodiversity in one of the world's most biodiverse regions.

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Nature Hike
experiences.description: Explore Costa Rica's most beloved national park with a certified naturalist guide who will help you spot white-faced capuchin monkeys, two-toed sloths, scarlet macaws, and the rare squirrel monkey. The hike winds through lush rainforest trails leading to stunning Pacific Ocean viewpoints and pristine white-sand beaches, perfectly blending wildlife with natural beauty.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 13:00. Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange private shuttle or shared transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort on the beachfront (approximately 3–4 hours depending on location). Enjoy the scenic coastal drive and take in your first views of Costa Rica's lush landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort, freshen up, and take a leisurely sunset stroll along the beach to get oriented. Explore the resort grounds and relax after the long journey.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport — try the local Sodas (small Costa Rican diners) inside the terminal for a casado (rice, beans, protein) for around $8–12
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's beachfront restaurant — enjoy fresh grilled fish or a traditional Gallo Pinto dish. Budget ~$20–30 per person

day_by_day.notes: Exchange some currency to Costa Rican Colones (CRC) at the airport for small purchases. Pre-book your shuttle transfer in advance. Keep Day 1 light as jet lag and travel fatigue will be a factor.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and enjoy a sunrise walk on the beach near the resort. After breakfast, join a guided mangrove kayaking tour along the nearby estuary — ideal for spotting herons, crocodiles, and howler monkeys in their natural habitat. Tours typically depart at 7:00–8:00 AM and last 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort and spend the afternoon snorkeling or swimming in the warm Pacific waters near the beachfront. Many mid-range resorts offer complimentary snorkel gear. Alternatively, explore the local village on foot or by bicycle rental (~$10/day).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a beach bonfire or hammock time at sunset. Head into the nearby town for dinner at a locally owned seafood restaurant along the waterfront promenade.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet or a la carte — eggs, fresh tropical fruits, Gallo Pinto. ~$12–18
meals.lunch: Casual beachside soda — try ceviche and patacones (fried plantains) for ~$10–15
meals.dinner: Waterfront seafood restaurant in town — grilled mahi-mahi or shrimp in garlic butter sauce. ~$18–28 per person

day_by_day.notes: Apply reef-safe sunscreen for all water activities. Book the mangrove kayak tour through the resort concierge the evening before to secure a spot.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning wildlife watching walk along a nearby nature trail or protected coastal reserve. Hire a local naturalist guide (~$30–40) to spot capuchin monkeys, sloths, scarlet macaws, and coatis. Best wildlife activity is between 6:00–9:00 AM when animals are most active.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby butterfly garden or reptile sanctuary for an educational eco-experience. These smaller attractions typically cost $15–25 and offer close-up encounters with poison dart frogs, iguanas, and exotic butterflies native to Costa Rica.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a local cultural experience — look for a traditional Costa Rican cooking class offered through the resort or a nearby eco-lodge. Learn to make Gallo Pinto, plantain dishes, and fresh tropical salsas.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the resort — granola, fresh fruit, and coffee before the wildlife walk. ~$10–15
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch packed by the resort or a local soda near the sanctuary — rice bowl with chicken and fresh salad. ~$10–12
meals.dinner: Cooking class includes dinner, or dine at a mid-range local restaurant — casado with beef or chicken. ~$15–20 per person

day_by_day.notes: Wear neutral-colored clothing (greens, browns, beige) for wildlife walks to avoid startling animals. Bring binoculars if available — they make a significant difference for birdwatching.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early by private shuttle or rental car toward Manuel Antonio National Park (travel time varies by resort location — approximately 1–3 hours). Arrive at the park gates by 8:00 AM to beat the crowds. Begin the Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Nature Hike with a certified naturalist guide who will identify sloths, monkeys, colorful birds, and coastal wildlife along the forested trails.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the guided hike, relax on the pristine white-sand beaches inside the national park — Playa Manuel Antonio is one of Costa Rica's most beautiful beaches. Swim, snorkel, or simply soak in the scenery surrounded by jungle.
day_by_day.evening: Drive or shuttle back toward the resort area. Stop in Quepos (the gateway town to Manuel Antonio) for dinner at a lively local restaurant before returning to the resort.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure — toast, eggs, and Costa Rican coffee. ~$12–15
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch or purchase from vendors near the park entrance — fresh fruit, sandwiches, and cold drinks. ~$8–12
meals.dinner: Dinner in Quepos at a mid-range restaurant — try the whole fried red snapper or shrimp pasta. ~$18–25 per person

day_by_day.notes: Manuel Antonio National Park limits daily visitors — book your guided nature hike and park entry tickets online in advance at sinac.go.cr. Park entry is ~$20 USD. The guide fee is typically $25–40 additional. Bring insect repellent and a dry bag for beach time.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning at the resort. Enjoy a slow breakfast, lounge by the pool, or indulge in a mid-range spa treatment such as a 60-minute Costa Rican coffee scrub or hot stone massage (~$60–80). This is a great recharge day mid-trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a surfing lesson on the beach with a local surf instructor (~$40–60 for a 2-hour group lesson including board rental). Costa Rica's Pacific coast offers excellent beginner-friendly waves, and February is prime surf season.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset yoga session on the beach (many resorts offer complimentary or low-cost classes). Follow with a casual dinner at the resort bar area — enjoy tropical cocktails and light bites while watching the stars emerge over the Pacific.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely resort breakfast — açaí bowl, fresh juices, and local cheeses. ~$15–20
meals.lunch: Beachside snack bar — fresh coconut water, empanadas, and ceviche. ~$8–12
meals.dinner: Resort bar and grill — wood-fired pizza or grilled chicken with plantain sides and a local Imperial beer. ~$18–25 per person

day_by_day.notes: This is an intentional rest day to maintain a balanced pace across the 13-day trip. Overloading every day leads to exhaustion — embrace the 'Pura Vida' lifestyle.

day_by_day.morning: Depart by shuttle or rental car toward Monteverde Cloud Forest Reserve — this is a longer transfer (approximately 4–5 hours depending on starting point). Depart by 6:00–7:00 AM to arrive in Monteverde by midday. The drive through Costa Rica's Central Valley and mountain roads is scenic and rewarding.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to a mid-range eco-lodge in Monteverde (pre-booked). After settling in, take a self-guided walk through the Santa Elena Cloud Forest Reserve — a less crowded alternative to the main Monteverde Reserve. Entry is ~$18. Spot quetzals, toucans, and cloud forest orchids.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a night walk in the cloud forest with a guided torch tour (~$25–35). Night walks reveal an entirely different ecosystem — tree frogs, tarantulas, stick insects, and nocturnal mammals like kinkajous.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure. ~$12–15
meals.lunch: Stop en route at a roadside soda in the Central Valley — try a traditional arroz con pollo (chicken and rice). ~$8–12
meals.dinner: Dinner at a cozy Monteverde restaurant — try the local trout (trucha) which is farm-raised in the cloud forest region. ~$18–25 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book your Monteverde eco-lodge accommodation well in advance as the area is popular. Pack a light rain jacket and layers — the cloud forest is significantly cooler and misty compared to the coast. Temperature can drop to 15–18°C (59–64°F) at night.

day_by_day.morning: The highlight of the trip — Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour. Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits. The tour typically includes 10–15 platforms, Tarzan swings, and a hanging bridge walk. Duration: 3–4 hours. Cost: ~$45–65 per person. Depart from the lodge at 7:30–8:00 AM for the first slot.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the zip-line adrenaline rush, visit the Monteverde Butterfly Garden and Hummingbird Gallery — a magical spot where dozens of hummingbird species feed at close range. Entry ~$15. Browse the local artisan market in Santa Elena town for handmade crafts and souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a local coffee or chocolate tour in the Monteverde area (~$20–25). Learn how cacao is harvested and processed into chocolate while sampling local varieties. End the evening with a relaxed dinner in town.

meals.breakfast: Eco-lodge breakfast — eggs, Gallo Pinto, fresh fruit, and locally grown Monteverde coffee. ~$12–18
meals.lunch: Café in Santa Elena town — try a bocas platter (Costa Rican tapas) with local cheese and bread. ~$10–15
meals.dinner: Mid-range restaurant in Monteverde — wood-oven chicken with yuca fries and a passion fruit dessert. ~$18–25 per person

day_by_day.notes: Wear closed-toe shoes and comfortable athletic clothing for the zip-line tour. Secure all loose items (glasses, hats, phones) before each zip. Minimum weight restrictions typically apply (check with operator). This is the signature adventure day of the trip!

day_by_day.morning: Early morning guided birdwatching walk in the Monteverde Cloud Forest Biological Reserve — the main reserve is home to over 400 bird species including the resplendent quetzal, one of the world's most spectacular birds. Best viewing is at dawn. Guide fee ~$30–40, reserve entry ~$25.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Monteverde Orchid Garden (entry ~$12) which houses over 450 orchid species, many of which are microscopic and viewable only through magnifying glasses. Visit the Monteverde Cheese Factory — a famous local institution that has been producing dairy products since the 1950s. Sample artisan cheeses.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Monteverde and begin the drive/shuttle toward the Arenal Volcano region (approximately 3–4 hours). Check in to a mid-range lodge near La Fortuna with views of the iconic Arenal Volcano.

meals.breakfast: Light early breakfast at the eco-lodge before the birdwatching walk. ~$10–15
meals.lunch: Cheese factory café in Monteverde — sandwiches with local cheese and fresh salads. ~$10–14
meals.dinner: La Fortuna restaurant upon arrival — try the local specialty of heart of palm salad and grilled beef tenderloin. ~$20–28 per person

day_by_day.notes: The resplendent quetzal is most commonly spotted between January and April during nesting season — February is an excellent time. Quetzal sightings are not guaranteed but your guide will maximize your chances. Arrive at the reserve gates by 6:00 AM.

day_by_day.morning: Morning hike on the Arenal Volcano lava fields trail — explore the solidified lava flows from the 1968 eruption with a local guide. The hike offers dramatic views of the volcano cone and surrounding rainforest. Duration: 2–3 hours. Cost: ~$30–45 with guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the La Fortuna Waterfall — a stunning 70-meter cascade accessible via a 500-step staircase descent (~15 minutes). Swim in the emerald pool at the base. Entry fee ~$20. The surrounding rainforest trail offers additional wildlife spotting opportunities.
day_by_day.evening: Soak in the famous Tabacón or Baldi Hot Springs — natural thermal pools heated by Arenal Volcano's geothermal activity. Mid-range entry with dinner buffet included is ~$60–80 per person. A perfect way to soothe muscles after hiking.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast with volcano views — eggs, rice, beans, tropical fruits. ~$12–18
meals.lunch: Picnic at the waterfall or a local soda in La Fortuna town — casado with fresh lemonade. ~$10–14
meals.dinner: Dinner buffet included at the hot springs resort — wide variety of Costa Rican and international dishes. Included in hot springs entry

day_by_day.notes: The La Fortuna Waterfall trail can be slippery — wear water shoes or sturdy sandals with grip. The descent is easy but the climb back up is strenuous. Budget extra time. Hot springs are most magical after dark when the volcano backdrop is illuminated.

day_by_day.morning: White-water rafting on the Río Sarapiquí or Río Toro near Arenal — these rivers offer Class II–IV rapids suitable for adventurous beginners to intermediate paddlers. Half-day tours depart at 8:00 AM and cost ~$55–75 per person including equipment, guide, and a light snack.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Arenal Hanging Bridges — a network of suspension bridges through primary rainforest offering spectacular canopy-level wildlife viewing. Self-guided entry ~$28, guided tours ~$45. Look for toucans, poison dart frogs, and howler monkeys.
day_by_day.evening: Return to La Fortuna town for a leisurely evening. Browse the local market, visit a small local brewery, or enjoy live music at a café. La Fortuna has a charming town square that comes alive in the evenings.

meals.breakfast: Early energizing breakfast at the lodge — protein-rich eggs, banana pancakes, and strong Costa Rican coffee. ~$12–18
meals.lunch: Post-rafting snack included with tour, followed by a proper lunch at a La Fortuna soda — chicken soup (sopa de pollo) and fresh fruit. ~$10–14
meals.dinner: Mid-range restaurant in La Fortuna town — try the local specialty of hearts of palm pasta or a traditional sancocho (hearty stew). ~$18–25 per person

day_by_day.notes: Confirm rafting difficulty level with the operator based on current river conditions — water levels vary seasonally. All safety equipment is provided. Non-swimmers should opt for Class II sections. Store valuables in the waterproof dry bag provided.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning wildlife boat tour on Lake Arenal or along the Río Frío near Caño Negro Wildlife Refuge (2-hour drive but worth it for serious wildlife enthusiasts). Alternatively, join a bird and wildlife watching tour on the shores of Lake Arenal — spot kingfishers, anhingas, caimans, and river otters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the journey back toward the Pacific coast and Aegean Bliss Resort (approximately 4–5 hours). Stop at a roadside fruit stand in the Central Valley to sample exotic tropical fruits — rambutan, starfruit, maracuyá (passion fruit), and fresh pineapple.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back at Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a welcome-back sunset on the beach and a relaxed dinner at the resort restaurant to decompress from the inland adventure segment of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Early lodge breakfast before departure. ~$12–15
meals.lunch: Roadside soda en route — traditional casado or a fresh fruit plate with local cheese. ~$8–12
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant dinner — grilled catch of the day with coconut rice and mango salsa. ~$20–28 per person

day_by_day.notes: This is a travel-heavy day — depart by 7:00 AM to avoid afternoon traffic through San José. Consider pre-booking a private shuttle for comfort on the long return journey (~$80–120 for a private van). Keep snacks and water in the vehicle.

day_by_day.morning: Full morning of ocean activities — join a dolphin and whale watching boat tour departing from the nearest marina. February falls within Costa Rica's humpback whale season (December–April) making this an exceptional time for sightings. Tour duration: 3–4 hours, cost ~$65–85 per person.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort and enjoy a final afternoon of relaxation on the beachfront. Rent a stand-up paddleboard (~$20/hour), collect shells, or simply hammock-read under a palm tree. Visit a local artisan market for last-minute souvenir shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory farewell dinner at the best mid-range restaurant in the area — choose a restaurant with outdoor seating and ocean views. Order a full Costa Rican feast: ceviche starter, grilled lobster or sea bass main, tres leches cake for dessert, and a round of guaro sours (local spirit cocktails).

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — full spread with fresh juices, tropical fruits, and made-to-order eggs. ~$15–20
meals.lunch: Light beachside lunch at the resort snack bar — fresh fruit smoothie bowl and a fish taco. ~$12–16
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner at a top local restaurant — budget ~$35–50 per person for a full celebratory meal with drinks

day_by_day.notes: Dolphin and whale watching is weather and sea-condition dependent. The captain may reschedule if seas are rough — confirm the morning of departure. Bring motion sickness medication if you are prone to seasickness. Tip your boat guide generously.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk on the beach — a quiet and reflective last morning in paradise. Pack bags and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. If time permits before the airport transfer, enjoy one last swim in the Pacific Ocean or a final cup of Costa Rican coffee on the resort terrace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrange airport transfer to Juan Santamaría International Airport (SJO) — allow ample travel time (3–5 hours depending on resort location) plus 3 hours before international departure for check-in and security. Purchase last-minute souvenirs at the airport duty-free — locally produced coffee, artisan chocolates, and handmade jewelry make excellent gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Costa Rica — carry the memories of 13 days of cloud forests, zip-lines, volcanoes, wildlife, and Pacific sunsets. Pura Vida!

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — go all out with a full tropical spread. ~$15–20
meals.lunch: Airport restaurant or café — a final casado or sandwich before boarding. ~$12–18
meals.dinner: On the plane or at a connection airport

day_by_day.notes: Confirm return flight details and airport transfer booking the night before. Costa Rica charges a departure tax (~$29 USD) which is typically included in modern airfare but verify with your airline. Leave a resort review and tip housekeeping staff. Reconfirm your flight status the morning of departure.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Costa Rica Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits. With over 13 cables and Tarzan swings, you'll glide above the treetops spotting howler monkeys, toucans, and exotic orchids. This iconic eco-adventure combines adrenaline with breathtaking biodiversity in one of the world's most biodiverse regions.

experiences.name: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari
experiences.description: Glide through the jungle canals of Tortuguero on a guided boat safari teeming with wildlife. Spot caimans, river otters, three-toed sloths, poison dart frogs, and over 300 bird species including the great green macaw. If visiting between July and October, witness the awe-inspiring nesting of endangered green sea turtles on the beach at night.

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Nature Hike
experiences.description: Explore Costa Rica's most beloved national park with a certified naturalist guide who will help you spot white-faced capuchin monkeys, two-toed sloths, scarlet macaws, and the rare squirrel monkey. The hike winds through lush rainforest trails leading to stunning Pacific Ocean viewpoints and pristine white-sand beaches, perfectly blending wildlife with natural beauty.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Hot Springs Experience
experiences.description: Walk among the rainforest canopy on a series of suspension bridges offering panoramic views of the iconic Arenal Volcano and surrounding jungle. Spot toucans, morpho butterflies, and howler monkeys from above the forest floor. End the day soaking in natural volcanic hot springs fed by geothermal activity, a uniquely Costa Rican eco-cultural experience.

experiences.name: Osa Peninsula Corcovado Rainforest Expedition
experiences.description: Venture into Corcovado National Park, described by National Geographic as 'the most biologically intense place on Earth.' A full-day guided trek through primary rainforest offers unmatched chances to see tapirs, pumas, harpy eagles, and all four Costa Rican monkey species. This remote, pristine wilderness is the ultimate bucket-list eco-adventure for serious wildlife enthusiasts.
experiences.location: Corcovado National Park, Osa Peninsula, Puntarenas Province

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Private airport transfer via luxury SUV to Aegean Bliss Resort. Upon arrival, enjoy a welcome cocktail and resort orientation. Settle into your beachfront suite and take a leisurely stroll along the private beach to decompress after travel.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on your private terrace or the resort's infinity pool bar overlooking the Pacific. Enjoy a relaxed welcome dinner at the resort's signature beachfront restaurant.

meals.breakfast: On the flight
meals.lunch: Light snack or meal at Juan Santamaría International Airport — try the airport lounge if available with your premium ticket
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort Signature Restaurant — fresh ceviche, grilled catch of the day with tropical fruit salsa, and a curated Costa Rican wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Arrange welcome amenities in advance: chilled champagne, tropical fruit basket, and a personalized itinerary booklet placed in the suite. Confirm all upcoming excursion bookings with your dedicated concierge upon arrival. Light packing for the evening — resort casual dress code.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise yoga session on the beach led by the resort's private instructor (6:30–7:30 AM). Follow with a lavish breakfast at the resort. Spend the late morning on a guided snorkeling excursion in the crystal-clear waters just off the resort's beachfront, exploring vibrant coral reefs and tropical marine life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private catamaran sailing charter along the Pacific coastline. Spot dolphins, sea turtles, and possibly humpback whales (February is peak whale season). Snorkeling stops at secluded coves included. Butler service with chilled drinks and fresh fruit on deck.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort for a private couple's or solo spa treatment at the resort wellness center — signature Costa Rican coffee scrub and volcanic mud wrap. Dinner at the resort's beachfront terrace under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Resort's open-air breakfast pavilion — tropical fruit platters, eggs Benedict with smoked marlin, freshly squeezed guanábana juice, and artisan Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic prepared by the resort chef, served aboard the private catamaran — lobster rolls, chilled gazpacho, artisan cheeses, and tropical fruit
meals.dinner: Beachfront candlelit dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort — grilled whole snapper, hearts of palm salad, plantain-crusted shrimp, and a local Guaro Sour cocktail

day_by_day.notes: Book the catamaran charter at least 48 hours in advance through the concierge. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a hat, and light layers for the sea breeze. February weather is typically dry season — expect sunny skies and calm seas, ideal for sailing.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning private wildlife walk along the resort's surrounding jungle trails with a certified naturalist guide. Spot scarlet macaws, howler monkeys, sloths, and iguanas in their natural habitat. The guide will provide expert ecological commentary on the biodiversity of the region.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer by private vehicle to Manuel Antonio National Park (approximately 20–45 minutes depending on resort location). Begin the **Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Nature Hike** — a premium private guided experience through lush rainforest trails leading to pristine white-sand beaches. Encounter white-faced capuchin monkeys, three-toed sloths, and poison dart frogs with your expert naturalist.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort. Freshen up and head to the resort's rooftop bar for sundowners. Dinner at a nearby acclaimed local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — açaí bowls, smoked salmon on sourdough, fresh tropical juices, and barista-crafted Costa Rican pour-over coffee
meals.lunch: Post-hike lunch at La Cantina de Manuel Antonio — a premium open-air restaurant near the park entrance. Try the casado de mariscos (seafood rice bowl) and fresh coconut water
meals.dinner: El Avión Restaurant, Manuel Antonio — set inside a retired 1954 Fairchild C-123 cargo plane, offering panoramic ocean views. Signature dishes: mahi-mahi in mango sauce, lobster thermidor, and local craft beers

day_by_day.notes: Manuel Antonio National Park limits daily visitor numbers — ensure advance reservations are made through the concierge. Wear lightweight moisture-wicking clothing, sturdy closed-toe shoes, and bring insect repellent. Binoculars are highly recommended and can be provided by the resort.

day_by_day.morning: Private early morning surf lesson on the resort's beach with a professional instructor (beginner to intermediate level). The Pacific coast in February offers excellent surf conditions. Follow with a refreshing freshwater rinse and a smoothie at the beach bar.
day_by_day.afternoon: Luxury transfer to a nearby private waterfall retreat — a hidden jungle waterfall accessible via a short guided hike. Swim in the natural pool beneath the falls, surrounded by pristine rainforest. A private picnic lunch is set up poolside by the resort team.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort. Enjoy a private tasting menu dinner prepared by the resort's executive chef — a curated Costa Rican gastronomy experience featuring locally sourced ingredients, farm-to-table philosophy, and paired with boutique Central American wines.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-surf breakfast at the resort beach bar — banana and almond butter toast, protein smoothie, and cold brew coffee
meals.lunch: Private picnic at the waterfall retreat — charcuterie board with local cheeses, cured meats, artisan breads, tropical fruit, and chilled sparkling water
meals.dinner: Resort Executive Chef's Private Tasting Menu (6 courses) — highlights include plantain soup with crème fraîche, sea bass ceviche with yuzu, slow-braised short rib with yuca purée, and a chocolate and coffee dessert flight featuring single-origin Costa Rican cacao

day_by_day.notes: The waterfall hike involves moderate terrain — wear comfortable hiking sandals or trail shoes. The private tasting dinner should be reserved 24 hours in advance with the resort's F&B team. Dietary restrictions and preferences can be accommodated with advance notice.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure via private charter flight or luxury ground transfer to the **Osa Peninsula** (approximately 1–1.5 hours by small aircraft from nearby airstrip, or 3–4 hours by road). Check into a premium eco-lodge base camp near Corcovado. Morning arrival orientation with local expedition guides.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the **Osa Peninsula Corcovado Rainforest Expedition** — an immersive afternoon entry into Corcovado National Park, described by National Geographic as 'the most biologically intense place on Earth.' Trek primary rainforest trails with a specialist naturalist guide. Encounter Baird's tapirs, peccaries, scarlet macaws, toucans, and potentially jaguar tracks. The Osa Peninsula hosts 2.5% of the world's biodiversity.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the premium eco-lodge. Debrief with guides over artisan cocktails. Dinner under the jungle canopy with ambient lighting, listening to the symphony of the rainforest.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure — eggs to order, fresh fruit, and strong Costa Rican coffee to fuel the travel day
meals.lunch: Gourmet trail lunch prepared by the eco-lodge — jungle sandwiches with local cheese and avocado, energy bars, and purified water with electrolytes
meals.dinner: Osa Peninsula eco-lodge open-air restaurant — locally caught fish tacos, hearts of palm salad, black bean soup, and a dessert of tres leches with tropical fruit compote. Pair with a local craft IPA or fresh agua de pipa (coconut water)

day_by_day.notes: Corcovado National Park requires advance permits — confirm all paperwork through your concierge before departure. Pack a dry bag with essentials: insect repellent (DEET-based recommended), rain poncho, binoculars, and a headlamp. River crossings may occur depending on trail selected — water shoes are advisable. This is a remote area with limited connectivity — embrace the digital detox.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day deep immersion into Corcovado. Dawn departure (5:30 AM) for the golden hour wildlife window — the best time to spot tapirs, monkeys, and exotic birds along the Sirena trail. Expert naturalist guide leads the expedition through primary old-growth rainforest with towering strangler figs and ancient ceiba trees.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Corcovado expedition into the afternoon. Visit a secluded Pacific beach within the park for a private picnic and a swim in the warm, pristine waters. Spot sea turtles nesting on the beach (February is active season). Guided mangrove kayaking along park waterways.
day_by_day.evening: Return to eco-lodge. A private outdoor massage treatment is arranged overlooking the jungle at sunset. Farewell dinner at the lodge with the expedition team.

meals.breakfast: Pre-dawn light breakfast at the lodge — granola, yogurt, and fruit with hot coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic on the Corcovado beach — grilled chicken wraps, fresh fruit salad, coconut water, and dark chocolate
meals.dinner: Eco-lodge farewell dinner — whole grilled snapper caught by local fishermen, patacones (fried green plantains) with guacamole, rice and beans cooked in coconut milk, and a local rum cocktail

day_by_day.notes: This is the most physically demanding day of the trip — wear broken-in hiking boots and moisture-wicking clothing. Apply sunscreen and insect repellent liberally. Hydration is critical in the humid jungle environment. Carry at least 2 liters of water per person.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning at the Osa eco-lodge. Optional sunrise birdwatching walk on the lodge's private nature trail. Enjoy a slow breakfast before private charter flight or transfer back toward the resort or to the next destination.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private transfer or charter flight to the **Tortuguero** region on the Caribbean coast (requires connection through San José or direct charter — approximately 1–2 hours by air). Check into a premium eco-lodge on the edge of Tortuguero National Park. Brief orientation with local guides.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the lodge's riverside deck, watching the jungle canals come alive at dusk. Spot caimans, river otters, and exotic birds from the comfort of the lodge terrace. Welcome dinner at the lodge restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Eco-lodge breakfast — gallo pinto (Costa Rican rice and beans), scrambled eggs with fresh herbs, fried plantains, and tropical juice
meals.lunch: In-flight snack box if traveling by charter, or a quick lunch at the San José transit lounge — fresh sandwiches and Costa Rican coffee
meals.dinner: Tortuguero eco-lodge restaurant — Caribbean-style whole snapper in coconut and ginger sauce, rice and beans cooked in coconut milk, fried yuca, and a fresh mango sorbet dessert

day_by_day.notes: Tortuguero is accessible only by boat or small aircraft — no roads connect to the town. Ensure all transfers are pre-arranged through the concierge. Pack a light rain layer as the Caribbean coast receives more rainfall than the Pacific. February can bring occasional showers — embrace the lush atmosphere.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn departure (5:00 AM) for the **Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari** — glide silently through the jungle canal network in a private electric boat to minimize disturbance to wildlife. Spot green iguanas, howler monkeys, Jesus Christ lizards, spectacled caimans, river otters, and an extraordinary array of tropical birds including toucans, herons, kingfishers, and the great green macaw.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the lodge for a late breakfast. Explore Tortuguero village on foot — a small, colorful Caribbean community with no roads. Visit the local turtle conservation center to learn about the sea turtle protection programs that have made Tortuguero famous. Optional afternoon kayak or stand-up paddleboard through secondary canals.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cocktails at the lodge bar. Private guided night walk along the beach to observe sea turtle nesting activity (February is green turtle season — subject to ranger-guided access and permit availability). Return for a late dinner celebrating the day's extraordinary wildlife encounters.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-safari snack (5:00 AM) — energy bar and coffee. Full breakfast upon return at 9:00 AM — eggs Benedict with Caribbean spiced hollandaise, fresh fruit, and strong coffee
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at a recommended local Tortuguero restaurant — rice and beans, plantains, and grilled fish with Caribbean spices
meals.dinner: Lodge private dining experience — lobster bisque, grilled Caribbean spiny lobster with herb butter, roasted vegetables, and a rum-infused crème brûlée

day_by_day.notes: Night turtle walks are strictly regulated by park rangers — group sizes are limited and red-light flashlights only are permitted to avoid disturbing nesting turtles. Confirm availability and permits through the lodge concierge. Bring waterproof footwear as the beach can be wet. Silence is mandatory during turtle encounters.

day_by_day.morning: Second morning wildlife boat safari along different canal routes within Tortuguero, focusing on deeper jungle waterways less frequented by tourists. Look for the elusive manatee, river dolphins, and rare bird species. Private guide provides expert ecological narration.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private charter flight or boat transfer to **Arenal Volcano** region (La Fortuna area) — approximately 2–3 hours by charter or 4–5 hours by private road transfer. Check into a premium Arenal-area lodge with volcano views. The iconic conical Arenal Volcano dominates the skyline as a dramatic backdrop.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at the Arenal luxury lodge and immediately head to the private volcanic hot springs on the property — soak in mineral-rich thermal pools while gazing at the illuminated Arenal Volcano at night. A truly magical Costa Rican experience.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast — gallo pinto, fresh tropical fruit, eggs to order, and Costa Rican specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch for the transfer — artisan sandwiches, fresh fruit, and cold brew coffee
meals.dinner: Arenal lodge restaurant — slow-cooked lamb with volcanic salt, roasted root vegetables, and a dessert of warm chocolate lava cake with vanilla ice cream. Pair with a premium Chilean Malbec

day_by_day.notes: The Arenal region offers one of Costa Rica's most iconic landscapes. The volcano is currently in a resting eruptive phase but remains an awe-inspiring presence. The hot springs are naturally heated by geothermal activity and are best enjoyed in the evening when the cooler night air contrasts with the warm mineral waters.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning guided hike on the **Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Hot Springs Experience** — traverse a series of suspension bridges through primary rainforest with panoramic views of Arenal Volcano and Lake Arenal. The canopy-level walkways provide exceptional birdwatching opportunities — spot toucans, motmots, and resplendent quetzals. Your private naturalist guide identifies flora and fauna throughout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Arenal experience with a private guided hike on the Arenal 1968 lava fields trail — walk across hardened lava flows from the historic 1968 eruption with the volcano as a dramatic backdrop. Afternoon soak in the premium Tabacón or Baldi hot springs resort — a world-class thermal spa experience with multiple pools at varying temperatures, swim-up bars, and lush tropical gardens.
day_by_day.evening: Return to lodge. Sunset cocktails on the volcano-view terrace. Private stargazing session with the lodge's astronomer guide — Arenal's low light pollution makes for spectacular night skies.

meals.breakfast: Early pre-hike breakfast at the lodge — oatmeal with tropical fruits, eggs, toast, and strong coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurante Nene's, La Fortuna — a beloved local institution serving authentic Costa Rican cuisine. Try the casado with grilled tilapia, rice, beans, and fresh salad
meals.dinner: Don Rufino Restaurant, La Fortuna — one of the region's finest restaurants. Signature tenderloin with chimichurri, hearts of palm carpaccio, and a decadent tres leches dessert. Excellent wine list

day_by_day.notes: The hanging bridges walk is approximately 3 km with moderate elevation changes — comfortable walking shoes are essential. The hot springs visit is best timed for late afternoon into evening for the most atmospheric experience. Book Tabacón Hot Springs in advance as capacity is limited.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early for **Monteverde Cloud Forest** — a scenic 3–4 hour private transfer from Arenal (partially via Lake Arenal boat crossing for a spectacular scenic route). Arrive at a premium Monteverde lodge nestled in the cloud forest. Check in and enjoy the mystical misty atmosphere of this unique ecosystem at 1,400 meters elevation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the **Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour** — one of Costa Rica's most exhilarating adventures. Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on a premium zip-line circuit featuring multiple lines, including a Superman-style line and a Tarzan swing. Speeds reach up to 80 km/h with breathtaking views over the forest canopy and surrounding valleys. Professional guides ensure maximum safety and excitement.
day_by_day.evening: Freshen up at the lodge. Guided night walk through the cloud forest reserve with a specialist naturalist — spot nocturnal species including kinkajous, olingo, glass frogs, and sleeping birds. The cloud forest at night is an otherworldly experience.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the Arenal lodge before departure — quick but hearty: eggs, gallo pinto, and coffee
meals.lunch: Scenic lunch during the Lake Arenal boat crossing — gourmet box lunch prepared by the Arenal lodge, enjoyed on the boat deck with volcano views
meals.dinner: Celajes Restaurant at a premium Monteverde lodge — creative cloud forest-inspired cuisine featuring local dairy (Monteverde is famous for its cheese), organic vegetables, and sustainably sourced meats. Try the chayote and cheese gratin and the cloud forest mushroom risotto

day_by_day.notes: The Lake Arenal boat crossing adds a spectacular dimension to the Arenal-Monteverde transfer — coordinate with your concierge to arrange this route. Monteverde is significantly cooler than the coast — pack a light fleece or jacket. The cloud forest is misty and atmospheric but can be chilly at night (15–20°C). The zip-line tour operates rain or shine — light rain actually enhances the mystical atmosphere.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided walk through the **Santa Elena Cloud Forest Reserve** or the **Monteverde Cloud Forest Biological Reserve** — explore the world-famous cloud forest with a specialist naturalist guide. Search for the resplendent quetzal, three-wattled bellbird, and the remarkable cloud forest ecosystem of orchids, bromeliads, and mosses. The reserve is home to over 400 bird species and 100 mammal species.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the **Monteverde Butterfly Garden** and **Hummingbird Gallery** — immersive encounters with hundreds of free-flying butterflies and dozens of hummingbird species feeding at close range. Afternoon cheese and coffee tasting at the historic **La Lechería (Monteverde Cheese Factory)** — established by Quaker settlers in the 1950s, producing world-class artisan cheeses in the cloud forest.
day_by_day.evening: Private transfer begins back toward the Pacific coast/resort area (3–4 hours, arriving late evening). Alternatively, spend one final night in Monteverde for a more relaxed schedule. Farewell dinner in Monteverde before departure.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast — cloud forest granola with local honey and Monteverde cream, fresh fruit, and specialty coffee grown on the Pacific slopes
meals.lunch: Café Caburé, Monteverde — a beloved artisan café and chocolate shop. Try the gourmet sandwiches, homemade truffles, and single-origin hot chocolate made from local cacao
meals.dinner: Morpho's Restaurant, Monteverde — a landmark local restaurant with an extensive menu of Costa Rican and international cuisine. Signature dishes include the chicken in Monteverde cream sauce and the chocolate fondue dessert

day_by_day.notes: The resplendent quetzal is most active in the early morning — start the reserve walk at 6:00 AM for the best chance of a sighting. Bring a telephoto lens if you have one, or rent binoculars from the reserve. The cheese factory tour is a fascinating cultural insight into Monteverde's unique Quaker heritage and is a must-do. Confirm return transfer timing with the concierge based on your final night preference.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at the Aegean Bliss Resort (if returned previous evening) or en route back to the resort. Leisurely final breakfast with ocean views. Last swim in the Pacific, final stroll along the beach. Collect any last souvenirs — premium Costa Rican coffee, artisan chocolate, and locally made handicrafts from the resort boutique.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relaxing spa session at the resort wellness center — final treatment to rejuvenate after 13 days of adventure: a signature Costa Rican coffee and coconut oil full-body massage. Pack and prepare for departure. Final afternoon by the infinity pool with a tropical cocktail.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the resort's finest dining venue — a celebratory meal to commemorate an extraordinary Costa Rican journey. Private transfer to Juan Santamaría International Airport arranged for overnight or early morning departure as needed.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent final resort breakfast — the full spread: smoked salmon, eggs Benedict, tropical fruit platters, fresh-baked pastries, and the finest Costa Rican coffee prepared by the resort barista
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch at the resort beach club — grilled fish tacos, fresh guacamole, and a final tropical cocktail (try the Guaro Sour with fresh lime)
meals.dinner: Resort signature farewell dinner — a curated 5-course tasting menu celebrating the flavors of Costa Rica: ceviche trio, sea turtle conservation-themed amuse-bouche, grilled lobster tail, a cheese course featuring Monteverde artisan cheeses, and a spectacular dessert of Costa Rican chocolate fondant with single-origin coffee ice cream. Toast with a glass of premium Champagne

day_by_day.notes: Confirm departure transfer timing with the concierge — Juan Santamaría International Airport is typically 2–3 hours from the Pacific coast depending on traffic. Allow ample time, especially if your departure is early morning on Day 14. Request a late checkout from the resort if your flight departs in the evening to maximize your final hours in paradise. Tip your guides, drivers, and resort staff generously — Costa Rican hospitality is extraordinary and gratuities are deeply appreciated.
